subject: Re: Pilot runway — top-up vs time extension and license tier alignment
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@stellarnet.io>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot runway and options

Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re close to an internal decision but have one practical ask: we’re hitting the pilot throughput ceiling and the team wants to either (A) buy a small top-up of 200k token-equivalent compute at the same pilot rate, or (B) extend the 30-day timebox by two weeks while keeping the existing token cap.

Couple of constraints from procurement: any price change needs a short amendment and we prefer not to upgrade to a full committed seat yet. Also, we need clarity on whether the current pilot license (Growth tier) would require a different SLA if we keep extending.

Can you outline the trade-offs (cost, impact on SLA, and how we’d sign the amendment)? If there’s a faster way (voucher/credit or add-on) we’d be open to that too.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Data Products, StellarNet
ops@stellarnet.io
From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@stellarnet.io>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot runway and options

Samir —

Appreciate the note. Short answer: both are doable; they just move different levers. High level:
- Top-up (200k tokens): immediate add-on, no change to timebox. We’ll issue a one-page amendment that increases the pilot credit pool. Pricing: $2,700 at our pilot rate (I’ll confirm exact math).
- Time extension (2 weeks): no token top-up, we extend the end date. Operationally simpler but risks the team hitting token caps later (depends on burst patterns).

SLA/licensing: extending the timebox doesn’t change the license tier or SLA. Moving to a dedicated seat or higher tier would be the point where different SLAs kick in.

I’ve looped in Laura (Sales Engineer) to confirm the perf/throughput estimate, and I’ll check with Markus (who signs off on concessions) on approval path for the top-up price. If you’re ok, I can send a compact amendment + signature link today.

Proposed next step: quick 20-minute call to pick top-up vs extension based on your usage spikes. When are you free?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot runway and options

Ben —

Checked the telemetry: StellarNet has consistent short bursts (30–90s) that trip concurrent token windows; a 200k token top-up will smooth the next two weeks for sure. If they want to avoid any risk of throttling, recommend top-up + keep the original end date. If they want more time to validate workflows, extension is OK but recommend adding a small burst allocation (50k) to avoid edge-case failures.

A couple of implementation notes for the amendment: include the exact token units, a one-sentence fallback (“If tokens are exhausted before the end date we will pause until amendment is executed”), and an acceptance checkbox for the customer to choose top-up vs extension on the DocuSign. I’ve attached an updated term sheet for Ben to send (pilot_term_sheet_v2.pdf).

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot runway and options — concession approval

Ben/Laura —

Approved the 200k token top-up at the pilot rate with a small concession: we’ll discount the add-on by 15% (final customer price $2,295) provided StellarNet agrees to a short SOW addendum and signs the amendment within 7 business days. Conditions:
1) No change to core SLA; pilot tier SLA stands.
2) If they request a third extension or conversion to a paid committed seat within 30 days, commercial will re-evaluate MSRP/discount.
3) Legal to add the fallback language Laura suggested and include the SOW_draft_StellarNet.docx as an exhibit.

If Ben is ready, send the amendment + DocuSign link and copy me. Keep the messaging tight: top-up = immediate runway; extension = lower admin, potential throttling if spikes continue.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Director, North America Sales — Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2026 17:36:00 -0700

Samir —

Thanks for the details and for the quick sync today. Per our conversation, here’s the compact option set I can send right now (attached amendment + SOW):

Option A — 200k token top-up (recommended for bursty workloads)
- One-time add-on at pilot rate, customer price: $2,295 (15% concession approved)
- Amendment: increases token pool and adds fallback sentence for exhaustion
- Signing: DocuSign link included; amendment effective upon signature

Option B — 14-day time extension (no token top-up)
- No cost change; pilot ends two weeks later
- Risk: if bursts continue they may experience temporary throttling until we agree a top-up

Attachments: pilot_term_sheet_v2.pdf, SOW_draft_StellarNet.docx
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567
DocuSign (amendment): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abc123

If you’d like, I’ll include a checkbox on the amendment for the customer to pick Option A or B; we find that speeds signing. Happy to jump on a 15-minute wrap-up call if the execs want to confirm.

Best regards,
